just_in.title: Dry-Roasted Poha Chivda: A Low-Oil Diwali Snack That Stays Crisp for Weeks
just_in.excerpt: Thin poha dry-roasted until crisp, then tossed with nuts and a mustard-seed tempering in just 3 tablespoons of oil — a complete sourced recipe for festive snacking without deep frying.
just_in.nri_angle: A make-ahead, shippable Diwali savoury for diaspora kitchens: one batch covers guests, gift jars and the tea tin, and keeps crisp for up to two weeks airtight.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Add thin poha in a wide pan. Dry roast on low flame till it is crisp. Keep it aside.
In the same pan heat oil. Add peanuts and roast till crisp.
Add cashew, roasted gram dal, dry coconut slices and roast for 3-4 minutes.
Then add raisin and roast till the raisins puff up. Keep the nuts aside.
In the same pan add mustard seeds and let it crackle.
Add green chili, curry leaves and saute till crisp and dry. Then add hing, turmeric, red chili powder, roasted nuts and mix well.
Now add nuts mixture to roasted poha along with salt, powdered sugar, aamchur powder and mix everything well.
Cool completely before storing; store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

steps: Add thin poha in a wide pan. Dry roast on low flame till it is crisp. Keep it aside.
In the same pan heat oil. Add peanuts and roast till crisp.
Add cashew, roasted gram dal, dry coconut slices and roast for 3-4 minutes.
Then add raisin and roast till the raisins puff up. Keep the nuts aside.
In the same pan add mustard seeds and let it crackle.
Add green chili, curry leaves and saute till crisp and dry. Then add hing, turmeric, red chili powder, roasted nuts and mix well.
Now add nuts mixture to roasted poha along with salt, powdered sugar, aamchur powder and mix everything well.
Cool completely before storing; store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

carousel.title: Melioidosis, a Deadly Soil Infection That Mimics TB, Is Going Undetected Across India
carousel.excerpt: A 15-centre Lancet study found the infection in 8.9% of high-risk hospital patients, and one in five died. The disease is not notifiable in India, labs routinely misidentify the bacterium, and standard TB treatment does not work against it.
carousel.image_caption: Colonies of Burkholderia pseudomallei, the soil bacterium that causes melioidosis, growing on Ashdown agar. The infection mimics tuberculosis and is going undetected across India.

sources.label: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

carousel.nri_angle: Diaspora families with diabetic parents in coastal and monsoon-soaked parts of India are the group most likely to meet this infection, and most likely to lose weeks to a wrong TB diagnosis first.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

items.note: The strongest risk factor; poor blood-sugar control sharply raises the risk of severe disease
items.text: People with diabetes
Chronic kidney or liver disease, or heavy alcohol use
Sickle cell disease or a weakened immune system

items.note: Farming, fishing, gardening and construction, especially during and after the monsoon
items.text: Regular contact with wet soil or surface water
Living in or travelling to coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Goa, Maharashtra or the Northeast

data_cards.catch_text: Diagnosis requires a laboratory culture. Standard TB medicines and many common antibiotics do not work against this bacterium.
